scene: At home, Dad begins screen-left and Child screen-right at a low animal-card table. Child is the four-year-old tiger boy in his unchanged yellow T-shirt and blue shorts. One small deck lies beside Dad and one distinct face-up tiger card lies in front of Child. An unobstructed route leads from their chairs across the same room to the doorway at frame-right. Use a locked 16:9 medium-wide two-shot that includes the table, both people and their route to the doorway. Dad stops play at the first bathroom signal and immediately helps departure begin; subsequent speech accompanies that departure. Never keep Child beside the game to finish English. No bathroom interior, toileting, return to the game, elapsed-time dissolve or extra person is shown.

emotion.baseline: Calm, warm and regulated baseline at ordinary family conversation volume. The need is expressed directly and Dad responds with matter-of-fact care.
emotion.allowed_shift: Child briefly checks that his turn will be saved and asks for company while already leaving. Dad reassures him with a small attentive nod and available presence; Child's thanks is quiet.
emotion.forbidden: No visible desperation, panic, bathroom dance, embarrassment, urgency comedy, shouting or frantic running. Dad must not bargain, demand a complete sentence, request another game move or wait for a further English line before stopping and helping him leave. Do not stretch the walk or freeze either character to fill time.

A.start: Dad and Child sit at the low table, Dad left and Child right. The deck rests beside Dad, and Child's single tiger card lies face-up in front of him. Their route toward the doorway at frame-right is clear; Dad's hands are near but not on the deck.
A.action: Dad briefly invites another round. At the first bathroom signal Dad immediately withdraws his hands from the cards, stops play and rises to help Child leave, without waiting for another Child line. Child rises during his own signal and begins moving away from the chair as Dad acknowledges the stop. Neither touches the deck or tiger card; do not ask permission to pause.
A.end: Both have risen and begun their first steps away from the table toward frame-right, with Dad to Child's left. Their chairs are behind them; the deck and face-up tiger card remain untouched in their original positions.

B.start: Both have risen and begun their first steps away from the table toward frame-right, with Dad to Child's left. Their chairs are behind them; the deck and face-up tiger card remain untouched in their original positions.
B.action: Continue the departure already begun in Part A. While walking at an ordinary comfortable pace, Child says he will return; Dad agrees and reassures him that his turn can wait. Child asks for company while both keep moving. Dad is already nearby and available, so this request is a check for reassurance, not a condition for receiving help. Do not stop to look at, rearrange or collect cards.
B.end: Child and Dad have moved farther along the clear route toward the doorway at frame-right, still with Dad to Child's left. Both are walking away from the table; the deck and tiger card remain fixed behind them.

C.start: Child and Dad have moved farther along the clear route toward the doorway at frame-right, still with Dad to Child's left. Both are walking away from the table; the deck and tiger card remain fixed behind them.
C.action: Dad confirms his company while continuing beside Child. Child thanks him during the departure, without turning back or stopping. Dad's final reassurance overlaps their remaining steps through the doorway; let the departure continue at a normal pace and never hold Child in frame for an extra beat. Keep each speaker's face visible for his own line, then let both leave the view naturally. The bathroom visit happens afterward off-screen; no return or resumed round is part of this lesson.
C.end: Child and Dad have left the room through the doorway at frame-right. The low table remains in view with the untouched deck and face-up tiger card exactly in place; the game is safely paused.
